gloss: how something comes out (in a photo); photographic result

definitions.gloss: how something comes out in a photo; photographic result
definitions.explanation: The way a subject appears when photographed — whether it looks good, clear, and well-lit. Combines {写|うつ}り (how something is captured) with {具合|ぐあい} (condition, state).

examples.japanese: {写真|しゃしん}の{写|うつ}り{具合|ぐあい}を{確認|かくにん}した。
examples.english: I checked how the photo turned out.

examples.japanese: {天気|てんき}によって{写|うつ}り{具合|ぐあい}が{変|か}わる。
examples.english: How photos come out changes with the weather.

examples.japanese: {証明|しょうめい}{写真|しゃしん}は{写|うつ}り{具合|ぐあい}が{気|き}になるので{何度|なんど}も{撮|と}り{直|なお}した。
examples.english: I was worried about how my ID photo would come out, so I retook it many times.

notes:
Combines {写|うつ}り (how a subject is captured on film or in a photo) with {具合|ぐあい} (condition, state). Describes how well something photographs — its lighting, clarity, and overall look in the finished image.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {写|うつ}り{具合|ぐあい}がいい: photographs well; comes out nicely
- {写|うつ}り{具合|ぐあい}を{確認|かくにん}する: to check how a photo came out

NOTE ON KANJI:
{写|うつ}り uses {写|しゃ} (to photograph or copy). For reflections in a mirror or images on a screen, the homophone {映|うつ}り ({映|うつ}り{具合|ぐあい}) is used instead.
